tipping_points.question: When you have a migraine, do you have to stop what you are doing and lie down?
tipping_points.intent: Determine if attacks are 'prostrating' (completely incapacitating, requiring bed rest in dark/quiet room).
tipping_points.definition: Prostrating: So severe that physical activity must stop and the person must lie down, usually in a dark, quiet room. The CFR requires attacks to be 'completely prostrating' for 30% or higher ratings.

options.label: Yes, I always have to stop everything and lie down in a dark/quiet room
Sometimes I have to lie down, but not always
No, I can usually power through the pain

tipping_points.question: How often do these PROSTRATING attacks happen?
tipping_points.intent: Determine frequency. 10% = avg 1 in 2 months. 30% = avg once a month. 50% = very frequent.
tipping_points.definition: Frequency is measured over 'the last several months' according to 38 CFR § 4.124a. Count only attacks that are completely prostrating.

options.label: More than once per month (2+ per month)
About once per month
About once every 2 months
Less than once every 2 months

tipping_points.question: Do these attacks cause you to miss work, lose income, or significantly affect your ability to work?
tipping_points.intent: Determine 'economic inadaptability' (required for 50% rating). This means attacks are so severe and frequent they prevent you from maintaining employment.
tipping_points.definition: Economic Inadaptability: The attacks are productive of severe economic consequences - missing work, losing jobs, or inability to maintain steady employment due to the frequency and severity of attacks.

options.label: Yes, I frequently miss work or have lost job opportunities because of migraines
Yes, I occasionally miss work or have reduced productivity
No, I manage to work despite the migraines

tipping_points.question: How long do these prostrating attacks typically last?
tipping_points.intent: Determine if attacks are 'prolonged' (lasting hours to days). This is required for 50% rating.
tipping_points.definition: Prolonged: Attacks lasting many hours or days. The 50% rating criteria specifically mentions 'prolonged' attacks.

options.label: 24+ hours (days)
4-24 hours
1-4 hours
Less than 1 hour

exam_tips: Bring a headache diary showing frequency over the last 6-12 months
Bring sick leave records or employer letters documenting missed work
Do NOT downplay symptoms - describe the worst attacks, not the best days
Use the word 'prostrating' if your attacks require you to stop and lie down
Mention associated symptoms: nausea, vomiting, photophobia (light sensitivity), phonophobia (sound sensitivity)

tipping_points.question: How often do you experience symptoms like panic attacks, severe anxiety, or flashbacks?
tipping_points.intent: Differentiate 30% (Occasional decrease in work efficiency) vs 50% (Reduced reliability/productivity) vs 70% (Deficiencies in most areas).
tipping_points.definition: Frequency and severity of symptoms determine the level of occupational and social impairment according to 38 CFR § 4.130.

options.label: Near-continuous symptoms that affect me daily
Multiple times per week
Occasionally (few times per month)
Rarely (less than monthly)

tipping_points.question: How do your symptoms affect your ability to work or maintain employment?
tipping_points.intent: Determine occupational impairment level. 30% = intermittent inability. 50% = reduced reliability. 70% = deficiencies in most areas.
tipping_points.definition: Occupational impairment ranges from occasional decrease in work efficiency (30%) to near-inability to function (100%).

options.label: I cannot work or have extreme difficulty maintaining any job
I work but with reduced reliability and productivity (miss days, poor performance)
I have intermittent periods where I cannot perform work tasks
I have occasional decreases in work efficiency

tipping_points.question: How do your symptoms affect your relationships with family, friends, or coworkers?
tipping_points.intent: Determine social impairment. This is a key factor in mental health ratings.
tipping_points.definition: Social impairment includes difficulty maintaining relationships, avoiding social situations, and inability to function in social settings.

options.label: I avoid almost all social contact and have no close relationships
I have very few relationships and frequently have conflicts or avoid social situations
I struggle with relationships and social situations but maintain some connections
I have occasional social difficulties but maintain relationships

tipping_points.question: Do you experience suicidal thoughts, severe depression, or inability to care for yourself?
tipping_points.intent: Identify high-level symptoms that indicate 70% or 100% ratings.
tipping_points.definition: Suicidal ideation, severe depression, and inability to perform activities of daily living are indicators of severe impairment.

options.label: Yes, frequently
Yes, occasionally
I have in the past, but not currently
No

exam_tips: Be completely honest - this is not the time to appear 'strong' or 'recovered'
Describe your worst days, not your best days
Mention sleep problems, nightmares, hypervigilance, avoidance behaviors
If you've lost jobs, relationships, or housing due to PTSD, mention it
Bring buddy statements from family/friends who witness your symptoms
If you have suicidal thoughts, ALWAYS mention this to the examiner

back_pain.condition_name: General Rating Formula for Diseases of the Spine

tipping_points.question: When you bend forward (flexion), how far can you go before pain stops you?
tipping_points.intent: Range of Motion (ROM) is THE primary rating factor for spine conditions. Forward flexion is measured from standing to the angle you can bend.
tipping_points.definition: Normal forward flexion: 90 degrees (fingertips to toes). 40% rating: 30 degrees or less. 20% rating: 30-60 degrees. ROM is measured to the point where pain STOPS you, not where you can push through.

options.label: 30 degrees or less (barely past my hips)
Between 30-60 degrees (somewhere between hips and knees)
60-90 degrees (past my knees but can't touch toes)
I can touch my toes (90 degrees)

tipping_points.question: Is the pain always present, even without movement?
tipping_points.intent: Determine if condition meets 'Intervertebral Disc Syndrome' (IVDS) criteria which can add to rating or qualify for separate rating.
tipping_points.definition: Incapacitating episodes: Pain so severe you cannot work or perform daily activities, requiring bed rest.

options.label: Yes, with frequent incapacitating episodes requiring bed rest (6+ weeks/year total)
Yes, with some incapacitating episodes (2-4 weeks/year total)
Yes, constant pain but no incapacitating episodes
Only with movement (painful motion)

tipping_points.question: Do you have radiating pain, numbness, or weakness in your legs?
tipping_points.intent: Identify radiculopathy (nerve involvement) which can add separate ratings or increase the spine rating.
tipping_points.definition: Radiculopathy: Nerve damage causing pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness along a nerve path (e.g., down the leg in sciatica).

options.label: Yes, severe symptoms with weakness/loss of reflexes
Yes, moderate pain/numbness radiating down leg(s)
Yes, mild occasional symptoms
No nerve symptoms

tipping_points.question: Does the pain affect your gait or require you to use assistive devices?
tipping_points.intent: Determine functional impact. Abnormal gait or need for assistive devices indicates higher level of impairment.
tipping_points.definition: Assistive devices: Cane, walker, wheelchair. Abnormal gait: Limping, inability to walk normally.

options.label: I use a wheelchair due to back pain
I use a cane or walker
I limp or have abnormal gait but no assistive devices
I can walk normally

exam_tips: CRITICAL: Stop at the point of pain during ROM testing - do NOT push through
The examiner will measure your ROM with a goniometer or inclinometer
ROM is measured on your worst day - tell the examiner if today is a 'good day'
Mention morning stiffness (how long until you can move normally)
Bring MRI/X-ray reports showing disc issues, stenosis, or other findings
If you have flare-ups, describe frequency and what triggers them
If you've modified your work duties or home life due to back pain, mention it

tipping_points.question: Do you experience ringing, buzzing, or other sounds in your ears that are not from an external source?
tipping_points.intent: Confirm tinnitus diagnosis. Tinnitus is rated at 10% only if recurrent.
tipping_points.definition: Tinnitus: Perception of sound (ringing, buzzing, hissing, roaring) when no external sound is present. Must be recurrent (not constant or never present).

options.label: Yes, it is constant (24/7)
Yes, it is frequent (daily or near-daily)
Yes, it is recurrent (several times per week)
Occasionally (less than weekly)

exam_tips: Tinnitus is rated at a flat 10% if recurrent - there is no higher or lower rating
The VA does not require objective evidence of tinnitus (it's subjective)
Mention if it affects your sleep, concentration, or daily activities
Mention if you use white noise machines, fans, or other coping mechanisms
If you have hearing loss separately, that is rated under different diagnostic codes

knee_pain.condition_name: Limitation of Flexion of the Knee

tipping_points.question: When you bend your knee, how far can you bend it before pain or stiffness stops you?
tipping_points.intent: Knee flexion ROM is the primary rating factor. Normal flexion is 140 degrees (heel to buttock).
tipping_points.definition: Normal knee flexion: 140 degrees. Ratings based on limitation: 30% = 45 degrees. 20% = 45-90 degrees. 10% = 90-110 degrees.

options.label: 45 degrees or less (very limited)
Between 45-90 degrees
Between 90-110 degrees
Normal or near-normal (110+ degrees)

tipping_points.question: Is your knee unstable (gives way, buckles, or feels like it might give out)?
tipping_points.intent: Instability can qualify for a separate rating under DC 5257 (recurrent subluxation or lateral instability).
tipping_points.definition: Instability: Knee gives way, buckles, shifts, or feels unstable during walking or activities. May indicate ligament damage (ACL, MCL, PCL, LCL).

options.label: Yes, severe and recurrent instability requiring a brace
Yes, moderate instability with frequent episodes
Yes, mild occasional instability
No instability

tipping_points.question: Do you experience swelling (effusion) in your knee?
tipping_points.intent: Chronic effusion can add additional percentage under DC 5260.
tipping_points.definition: Effusion: Fluid buildup in the knee joint causing visible swelling.

options.label: Yes, persistent swelling (always present)
Yes, recurrent swelling (comes and goes)
No swelling

exam_tips: The examiner will measure knee flexion with a goniometer
If you wear a knee brace, mention why (instability, pain control, etc.)
Bring imaging reports (MRI showing meniscus tears, ligament damage, arthritis)
Mention if you've had surgery (meniscectomy, ACL repair, etc.)
If the knee gives out, describe specific incidents
You may qualify for multiple separate ratings (flexion limitation + instability + arthritis)
